title: Returns done right: absolute, CAGR, XIRR, trailing, rolling
objectives: Convert an absolute return into CAGR for a lump sum and XIRR for a SIP.
Explain why point-to-point and trailing returns can flatter a fund.
body_md:
Absolute return is total gain ignoring time: ₹1 lakh → ₹2 lakh is 100% absolute. CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate) is the steady yearly rate for a single lump sum: ₹1 lakh → ₹2 lakh in 5 years is about 14.9% a year, not 20%. XIRR is the annualised return when money goes in or out on different dates — the right measure for SIPs. Point-to-point return depends on the two dates chosen; trailing return is measured up to today over 1, 3 or 5 years; rolling returns average many overlapping periods and show consistency.

| Term | Plain meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Absolute return | Total gain as a percentage, ignoring time | ₹1 lakh → ₹2 lakh = 100% absolute return |
| CAGR | Compound Annual Growth Rate: the steady yearly rate that turns the start value into the end value. Right for a single lump sum | ₹1 lakh → ₹2 lakh in 5 years ≈ 14.9% CAGR, not 20% a year |
| XIRR | The annualised return when money goes in or out on different dates. Right for SIPs | A 3-year SIP shows 40% absolute, but XIRR may be about 22% |
| Point-to-point return | Return between two chosen dates; can look very good or very bad depending on the dates | Return from a market low looks flattering |
| Trailing return | Return up to today over 1, 3, 5 years | "5-year return as of 30 Sep" |
| Rolling returns | Average of many overlapping periods (e.g. every 3-year window over 10 years); shows consistency | Fund beat benchmark in 80% of 3-year windows |

> **Talk-track:** “Your statement shows a big absolute number. Let's turn it into XIRR so you can compare it fairly with a fixed deposit or the index.”
example: A 3-year SIP shows 40% absolute, but its XIRR may be about 22% — quote the annualised figure, with the period stated.
say: 100% in 5 years is not 20% a year; it is about 14.9% CAGR.
For SIPs use XIRR; for lump sums use CAGR.
never: A 100% return over 5 years means 20% a year.
A SIP's absolute return is the right yearly figure.

check.q: Which return measure suits a SIP?
check.why: XIRR. XIRR handles money invested on different dates.
